clue.text: Empress who danced briefly until confined by parents

indicators.note: being confined by something means sitting inside it, so the parents wrap round the other piece

parts.note: mother and father are MA and DA, informal names for parents
mother and father are MA and DA, informal names for parents

indicators.note: the word until is cut short, losing its opening letters to give its informal shortening

explanation.surface: A history note about an empress who danced until her parents kept her locked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' clips the start of 'until' and 'confined by' puts the result inside the two parents. The definition joins the twelfth-century Empress Matilda to the Australian song 'Waltzing Matilda'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Empress Matilda was a medieval claimant to the English throne, and the waltzing girl in the famous Australian song bears the same name.

clue.text: Quite besotted with an amorous student?

parts.note: the indefinite article gives A
L, the learner plate, stands for a student
someone amorous is a lover

explanation.surface: Someone is completely smitten with a romantically inclined student.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' marks the loose step from 'amorous' to LOVER. Being 'all over' someone is an idiom for showing them heavy affection, so the definition is 'Quite besotted with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all over a person is an idiom for fawning on them with obvious, total infatuation.

clue.text: The man who wants his d____?

definitions.text: The man who wants his d____?

parts.words: The man who wants his d____?
parts.note: the gap after the d must be filled to make a meal word, and the phrase for appetite, 'the ___ man', is the man who wants that meal

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank puzzle about a hungry man.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'inner man' is a jocular phrase for the stomach or appetite, and the missing letters after the d complete the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner man is an old idiom for one's appetite, the self that wants feeding.

clue.text: 's missing from audible check on oil painting

indicators.note: one letter is absent from the gauge word, so it is taken away
audible tells us the result is said aloud and spelt as another word with that sound

parts.note: a dipstick is the rod used to check the oil level in an engine
the clue's opening 's stands for the letter S

explanation.surface: Something is missing when the oil is checked within earshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audible' says the oil gauge's name is heard as DIPSTYCH; 'missing from' then removes the S, which comes from the clue's opening "'s". 'missing from' works on the sounded word, not the written one.
explanation.definitionFit: A diptych is a painting made on two hinged panels, often an altarpiece.

clue.text: Back number is in time to suffer

indicators.note: in places the reversed number and IS inside the time word

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for number is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A complaint that some old number is taking a long time to get through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses the abbreviation for number, and 'in' puts that and IS inside the time word. 'Back' looks like part of the surface's 'back number' (an old issue) but only signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to undergo great mental anguish, so it can stand in for suffer.

clue.text: Instrument protector nearly keeping it

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the shortened word wraps the other piece
nearly drops the last letter of the protector word

parts.note: a guard is something that protects
taken as written

explanation.surface: A case that almost covers a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' clips the protector's last letter and 'keeping' wraps what remains round 'it', which is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The guitar is a stringed musical instrument that is plucked or strummed.

clue.text: Exciting event at one's finger-tips?

definitions.meaning: a tense, close-run contest that keeps an audience on edge
read literally, someone who gnaws at the tips of their fingers

explanation.surface: A thrilling occasion described as being close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At one's fingertips' usually means readily available; here it means someone literally chewing their fingertips.
explanation.definitionFit: A tense contest is called this because it makes spectators chew their nails anxiously.

clue.text: Little girl pursues wrongdoing till further notice

indicators.note: pursues means comes after, so the girl's name follows the wrongdoing

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
Edie is a pet form of the girl's name Edith

explanation.surface: A small girl chases after some mischief, with no end in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursues' puts the girl's name after the wrongdoing. Sine die is Latin, 'without a day', and is used of a meeting adjourned with no date set to resume.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means adjourned with no fixed date, that is indefinitely.

clue.text: Writer of passages about wild bull

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the river crossings go round the other pieces

parts.note: fords are shallow passages across rivers
the second river crossing in the plural
wild means mad
an ox is a bovine animal like a bull

explanation.surface: A writer of passages about a wild bull, perhaps an author of animal stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passages' gives two river crossings and 'about' puts them round the wild bull. Ford Madox Ford was the English novelist who wrote The Good Soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford Madox Ford was an English novelist and editor, author of The Good Soldier.

clue.text: Map chap — that's resonant

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram
a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: Someone praises a map-maker for his ringing tones.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, deep, resonating sound, often a mournful one.

clue.text: Do well without turning nice and skilful

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the do-well word goes round the rest

parts.note: to profit is to do well or benefit

indicators.note: turning means the letters of nice are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone manages to succeed without becoming nice, and is good at it too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: the do-well word goes round the letters of 'nice' rearranged by 'turning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proficient means competent and expert, which is to say skilful.

clue.text: Shroud for setter is 15 24

definitions.meaning: a shroud is laid on top of a corpse, and the setter speaks of himself as 'my'
the entry refers to the linked answer at 15 and 24, a phrase of firm refusal

explanation.surface: The setter calls a shroud for himself an emphatic refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: A shroud lies over a dead body, so for the setter it lies over his own. The phrase is also a vehement refusal, like the cross-referenced answer at 15 and 24.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are emphatic declarations of refusal to allow something to happen.

clue.text: See 12
I put ink to paper — hence remove copy in the commercial

parts.note: a print is a copy

indicators.note: remove takes away the letter that the copy word and the commercial phrase would share

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, so the phrase gives THE AD

explanation.surface: A printer explains that it removes a copy from an advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: The copy is set into THE AD so that its T doubles as the T of THE: 'remove' drops that second T and 'hence' is a link. The definition reads as the part speaking for itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A printhead is the part of a printer that deposits ink onto the page.

clue.text: Statement of resistance giving advance warning — three quarters reach nearly the infernal abyss

indicators.note: only three quarters of the twelve letters stay, so a run of three is dropped

parts.note: a notification is an advance warning

indicators.note: nearly drops the final letter of the infernal word

parts.note: the infernal regions are hell
a pit is an abyss

explanation.surface: A protest gives warning that it has nearly reached the bottomless pit of hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three quarters' keeps nine of the warning word's twelve letters by dropping a central run of three; 'nearly' clips the infernal word. 'giving' and 'reach' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you will stop it if you can is a declaration of resistance.

clue.text: Guide on the ranch?

definitions.meaning: to direct or pilot a course
a young bullock of the kind raised on a cattle ranch

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a guide on a cattle ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is an example, so it ends in '?': cattle on a ranch include castrated young bulls.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to guide, and a steer is a castrated bullock raised for beef on a ranch.

clue.text: Stone's first entry

parts.note: A is first in the alphabet and stands for first-class
a gate is a way of entry

explanation.surface: A stone marking the first way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious stone, a form of chalcedony.

clue.text: Leave posh beat in a stew

parts.note: to go is to leave
U means upper-class, the opposite of non-U
to lash is to beat or whip

explanation.surface: Upper-class people beat a retreat when things get chaotic.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class (or 'posh') comes from the old U and non-U classification of English usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Goulash is a Hungarian stew of meat seasoned with paprika.

clue.text: Limit prisoner's following …

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
the 's of the clue gives S
a train is a following or retinue

explanation.surface: A convict's band of followers is restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, where the same TRAIN reappears.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to restrict or limit someone's freedom.

clue.text: Waste silk product of science to take place unfinished

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for science

indicators.note: unfinished drops the last letter of the take-place word

parts.note: to happen is to take place

explanation.surface: A recycled silk item is the result of science that never quite comes about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' clips the last letter of the take-place word. 'Waste silk' is a technical term, not an instruction to throw silk away; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Schappe is a yarn spun from the waste silk left over after reeling.

clue.text: 2 28s then find part of Tahiti with unlikely weather

indicators.note: part of says the letters are hiding inside the island's name

parts.note: snow would be most improbable on a tropical island

explanation.surface: People who believe it is finished discover a strange snowfall in the South Seas.
explanation.walkthrough: '2 28s' are ALL OVER THINKERs: in the 1966 World Cup final, England's football win, the BBC commentator said 'They think it's all over... it is now!'
explanation.definitionFit: The famous commentary line answers those who think it's all over by saying the game is now truly over.

clue.text: Lets us out of contention

indicators.note: out of here means the letters of lets us are put out of order and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone excuses us from an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is the anagram indicator, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous struggle or scuffle, a contention between parties.

clue.text: … which makes commercials

parts.note: a puff is a piece of promotional advertising
a second puff, for the plural

explanation.surface: Something is responsible for producing adverts.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 19, so 'which' means the TRAIN there, and puff-puff is a child's word for a steam train. 'makes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Puff-puff is nursery talk for a steam train, the following referred to back in 19.

clue.text: See 15
Fast mover's lung? (I'm not serious)

definitions.meaning: nothing travels faster than the radiation from the sun
butchers call animal lungs by this name, so one is a single lung
a remark said in a playful, frivolous way

explanation.surface: Someone jokes about a speedy runner's lungs.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the fastest thing there is, an old word for an animal's lung, and the not-serious tone the brackets announce.
explanation.definitionFit: Light is the fastest thing known, lights are offal lungs, and light means not serious.

clue.text: Look at beat — it helps to keep time

parts.note: to watch is to look at
to strap is to beat with a strap

explanation.surface: A drummer is told to watch the beat to stay in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep time' sounds like keeping a beat in music, but the strap holds the timepiece on the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A wristband holds a timepiece on the arm, helping the wearer keep it with them.

clue.text: See 10
Rodin's work is unconvincing to royals

parts.note: a thin excuse is unconvincing
K is the abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A critic says Rodin's sculpture fails to impress the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royals' gives two of them, K (king) and ER (the Queen).
explanation.definitionFit: The Thinker is Auguste Rodin's famous bronze sculpture of a seated man in thought.

clue.text: Won't clue Telford, say?

parts.note: reading the answer as an instruction, a new arrangement of the letters of town makes won't, which is the clue

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to give a hint about Telford.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay, new (rearranged) town, gives WONT. TELFORD is a post-war planned town in Shropshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Telford is an English planned town built after the war, one example of the type.
